newsitem.title: SWITZERLAND: Aznavour, rock, jazz stars set for Montreux fete.
newsitem.headline: Aznavour, rock, jazz stars set for Montreux fete.

text.p: French singer Charles Aznavour and U.S. singer-pianist Ray Charles are among the stars who will perform at this year's world-renowned Montreux Jazz Festival, organisers announced on Thursday.

Also appearing at the festival, which has swung from presenting pure jazz to covering a wide range of popular and ethnic music over the past two decades, will be rhythm-and-blues star B.B.King and rock guitarist Eric Clapton.
The jazz tradition at the two-week event from July 4-19 will be represented by pianist Herbie Hancock and Swiss pianist Thiery Lang and his trio.
Rock and soul groups to appear will include the U.S. bands Supertramp and Earth, Wind and Fire.

Festival founder Claude Nobs told a news conference that Aznavour, who lives in Switzerland, would be presenting a programme of songs going back 50 years with other stars including Patti Austin from the United States.
Other highlights will be a Brazilian weekend, with a wide range of groups representing the country's musical styles, and an Irish evening with the Dublin folk group, The Chieftains.
